content.value_statement: Writing complete test scaffolds takes time and consistency. This skill creates pytest templates that follow TDD structure and project conventions.
actual_capabilities: Creates pytest test outlines for modules, functions, classes, fixtures, and async functions.
Uses provided templates for function, class, parametrized, async, and fixture tests.
Organizes tests with Arrange, Act, Assert sections and descriptive docstrings.
Suggests happy path, edge case, error handling, and parametrized test cases.
Provides a summary of generated test classes, functions, fixtures, and next steps.
limitations: Generated tests still need real assertions and project-specific test data.
It depends on source files or clear user descriptions for accurate coverage.
It does not prove tests pass unless the user runs the project test suite.
It is focused on pytest-style Python projects and may need adaptation for other frameworks.

use_cases.title: Start Tests For A New Module
use_cases.description: Generate a structured pytest file before implementing a new Python module.

use_cases.title: Standardize Project Test Style
use_cases.description: Create tests that follow existing TDD conventions, docstring rules, and type hint expectations.

use_cases.title: Prepare Fixture And Async Coverage
use_cases.description: Draft fixture and async test scaffolds for services that need setup, teardown, or concurrent behavior checks.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Basic Function Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for one named function.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate pytest tests for the validate_email function with happy path, edge case, and invalid input coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Module Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for a source file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read src/python_modern_template/validators.py and generate a matching pytest file using project TDD conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Class Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate pytest tests for UserManager with fixtures for initialization and tests for create, delete, and find behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Async Parametrized Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for async behavior and multiple cases.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate async pytest tests for fetch_data with parametrized success, timeout, HTTP error, and concurrent execution cases.

output_examples.input: Generate tests for a validate_email function.
output: A pytest test class for validate_email.
Separate cases for valid emails, invalid formats, empty input, and special characters.
A short summary of created tests and suggested next steps.

output_examples.input: Generate tests for a UserManager class.
output: A pytest class with a reusable UserManager fixture.
Tests for initialization, create_user, delete_user, and find_user behavior.
TODO markers where real project data and assertions are required.
Async pytest cases for a successful response and error paths.
A concurrent execution scenario using the project async test pattern.
Guidance to replace placeholders with service-specific expectations.

best_practices: Read project testing documentation before generating new test files.
Replace every TODO with concrete data, expected results, and assertions.
Run tests after generation to confirm the intended TDD red phase.
anti_patterns: Do not accept generated placeholders as finished tests.
Do not mock internal business logic that should be tested directly.
Do not generate broad tests that verify multiple unrelated behaviors at once.

faq.question: Which test framework does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets pytest for Python projects and follows the templates included with the skill.

faq.question: Can it create tests from an existing source file?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks the assistant to read the source file, inspect public functions and classes, and create matching tests.

faq.question: Does it write complete passing tests?
faq.answer: It creates structured boilerplate. Users must add real inputs, expected results, and project-specific assertions.

faq.question: Can it generate fixture templates?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a fixture template with setup, yield, and teardown sections.

faq.question: Can it help with async functions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes async pytest patterns and concurrent execution examples.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
